Bayesian estimation of linear-bilinear models: AMMI and SREG (GGE)

Source: R/bayes_ammi.R
bayes_ammi.Rd

bayes_ammi() estimates the linear-bilinear models of a multi-environment trial by the general Bayesian method of Perez-Elizalde et al. (2012): the additive main effects and multiplicative interaction (AMMI) model and the sites regression (SREG, GGE) model. The data of an earlier trial with the same genotypes and environments can be the prior (.prior_data): its cell means, effects and singular value decomposition give conjugate priors whose weight is its number of replicates, as in the paper's analysis of two years of a maize trial. Without an earlier trial the priors are vague but proper. The sampler is compiled (C++); every parameter has a posterior distribution, and bayes_ammi_biplot() draws the biplot with highest posterior density (HPD) regions.

Usage

bayes_ammi(
  .data,
  .y,
  .gen,
  .env,
  .rep,
  .nIter = 1000L,
  .prior_data = NULL,
  .n0 = NULL,
  .model = c("AMMI", "SREG", "GGE"),
  .k = NULL,
  .burnin = 0L,
  .thin = 1L,
  .chains = 1L,
  .priors = bys_priors(),
  .level = 0.95,
  .seed = NULL,
  .align = TRUE,
  .waic = TRUE
)

# Default S3 method
bayes_ammi(
  .data,
  .y,
  .gen,
  .env,
  .rep,
  .nIter = 1000L,
  .prior_data = NULL,
  .n0 = NULL,
  .model = c("AMMI", "SREG", "GGE"),
  .k = NULL,
  .burnin = 0L,
  .thin = 1L,
  .chains = 1L,
  .priors = bys_priors(),
  .level = 0.95,
  .seed = NULL,
  .align = TRUE,
  .waic = TRUE
)

Arguments

.data

a data frame with one row per plot.

.y, .gen, .env, .rep

the columns of the response, genotypes, environments and replicates: bare names or strings. The same names are used in .prior_data.

.nIter

number of iterations kept per chain before thinning (after the burn-in).

.prior_data

NULL (default: vague priors) or a data frame of an earlier trial with the same columns, genotypes and environments, used as prior (Perez-Elizalde et al. 2012).

.n0

weight of the earlier trial: the number of its observations per cell in the prior (default its number of replicates).

.model

"AMMI" (default) or "SREG" (sites regression, GGE; "GGE" is accepted).

.k

number of bilinear terms \(K\) (default NULL: all of them).

.burnin

number of iterations discarded at the start of every chain (default 0).

.thin

keep every .thin-th iteration (default 1).

.chains

number of chains (default 1).

.priors

the vague priors used without an earlier trial, from bys_priors().

.level

probability of the HPD intervals (default 0.95).

.seed

integer seed for a reproducible run, or NULL; the random number state of the session is restored afterwards.

.align

keep the sign of every bilinear term (default TRUE).

.waic

compute WAIC during sampling (default TRUE).

Value

An object of class c("bys_bayes_ammi", "bys_result", "list"); the components of version 0.2.0 come first, the draws of all chains one after the other:

mu1

data.table, column mu: draws of the overall mean.

tau1

data.table, column tau: draws of the error variance \(\sigma^2\).

tao1

data.table, columns tao1, ..., taoG: draws of the genotype effects (no columns for SREG).

delta1

data.table, columns delta1, ..., deltaE: draws of the environment effects.

lambdas1

data.table, columns lambdas1, ...: draws of the singular values.

alphas1, gammas1

data.tables, one row per draw, columns alphas1, ..., alphas<GK> (genotype scores, genotypes within terms) and gammas1, ... (environment scores).

Mean_Alphas, Mean_Gammas

data.tables, columns V1, ..., VK: posterior means of the score matrices.

summary

data.table: posterior mean, standard deviation, Monte Carlo standard error, HPD interval, effective sample size and potential scale reduction factor of every parameter.

scores

data.table: posterior means of the biplot coordinates.

draws

coda::mcmc.list of all parameters.

diagnostics

Gelman-Rubin, Raftery-Lewis and Heidelberger-Welch diagnostics.

ls

least-squares fit of the trial; prior: the fit of the earlier trial used as prior.

fit

DIC and WAIC.

settings

iterations, burn-in, thinning, chains, terms, model, priors, level, seed, time used.

Methods: print(), summary(), plot(), bayes_ammi_biplot(), bys_interpret(), bys_compare(), bys_cite().

Details

Models. For genotype \(i\), replicate \(l\) and environment \(j\), $$\textrm{AMMI: } y_{ijl} = \mu + \tau_i + \delta_j + \sum_{k=1}^{K} \lambda_k \alpha_{ik} \gamma_{jk} + e_{ijl}, \qquad \textrm{SREG: } y_{ijl} = \mu + \delta_j + \sum_{k=1}^{K} \lambda_k \alpha_{ik} \gamma_{jk} + e_{ijl},$$ \(e_{ijl} \sim N(0, \sigma^2)\), with \(\sum_i\tau_i = \sum_j\delta_j = 0\), \(\lambda_1 \ge \cdots \ge \lambda_K > 0\), and orthonormal score matrices \(\mathbf{U} = (\boldsymbol{\alpha}_k)\) and \(\mathbf{V} = (\boldsymbol{\gamma}_k)\), \(\mathbf{U}^\top\mathbf{1} = \mathbf{0}\), and for AMMI also \(\mathbf{V}^\top\mathbf{1} = \mathbf{0}\) (paper, eq. 1.2-1.3). By default all \(\min(G, E) - 1\) terms are fitted (\(\min(G - 1, E)\) for SREG), as in the paper and the earlier versions; .k fits fewer.

An earlier trial as prior (.prior_data). With \(n_0\) its number of replicates (.n0), \(\mathbf{Y}_0\) its table of cell means and \(\mu_0\), \(\boldsymbol{\tau}_0\), \(\boldsymbol{\delta}_0\), \(\mathbf{U}_0\mathbf{D}_0 \mathbf{V}_0^\top\) its least-squares fit (paper, Section 2.2): $$\mu \sim N\left(\mu_0, \frac{\sigma^2}{n_0 GE}\right), \quad \mathbf{K}_G\boldsymbol{\tau} \sim N\left(\mathbf{K}_G\boldsymbol{\tau}_0, \frac{\sigma^2}{n_0 E}\mathbf{I}\right), \quad \mathbf{K}_E\boldsymbol{\delta} \sim N\left(\mathbf{K}_E\boldsymbol{\delta}_0, \frac{\sigma^2}{n_0 G}\mathbf{I}\right),$$ \(\lambda_k \sim N(\lambda_{0k}, \sigma^2/n_0)\) truncated to the order (eq. 2.9), von Mises-Fisher priors \(p(\mathbf{U}) \propto \mathrm{etr}(n_0\mathbf{Y}_0\mathbf{V}_0 \mathbf{D}_0\mathbf{U}^\top/\sigma^2)\) and \(p(\mathbf{V}) \propto \mathrm{etr}(n_0\mathbf{Y}_0^\top\mathbf{U}_0\mathbf{D}_0\mathbf{V}^\top/\sigma^2)\) (eq. 2.7-2.8), and \(a S^2_0/\sigma^2 \sim \chi^2_a\) with \(a = n_0 - 1\) and \(S^2_0\) the within-cell mean square of the earlier trial (eq. 2.11; the values of the earlier versions of the package).

Conditional distributions (paper, Section 2.3). With \(\mathbf{Y}\) the cell means of the trial, \(B\) its replicates and \(n = BGE\), the linear effects are normal with means \((n\bar{y} + n_0GE\mu_0)/(n + n_0GE)\) and so on; the singular values are truncated normal with mean \((B\,\boldsymbol{\alpha}_k^\top\mathbf{Y}\boldsymbol{\gamma}_k + n_0\lambda_{0k})/(B + n_0)\) and variance \(\sigma^2/(B + n_0)\) (eq. 2.15); the score matrices are von Mises-Fisher (eq. 2.13-2.14), drawn one column at a time on the sphere orthogonal to \(\mathbf{1}\) and the other columns (Hoff 2009) with parameters \((B\lambda_k\mathbf{Y}\boldsymbol{\gamma}_k + n_0\lambda_{0k}\mathbf{Y}_0\boldsymbol{\gamma}_{0k})/\sigma^2\) and the same for \(\mathbf{V}\); and $$\sigma^2 \sim \frac{aS^2_0 + \mathrm{SSW} + B\sum_{ij}(\bar{y}_{ij} - \hat{y}_{ij})^2}{\chi^2_{a + n}}.$$ As in the paper, the dependence of the priors on \(\sigma^2\) is left out of its conditional distribution (it would involve the normalising constants of the von Mises-Fisher priors). Without an earlier trial the priors of bys_priors() apply, which do not depend on \(\sigma^2\), and all conditionals are exact (Crossa et al. 2011).

Starting values and signs. With an earlier trial the first chain starts at its least-squares fit and every draw keeps the orientation of its score vectors (.align); otherwise the first chain starts at the least-squares fit of the trial. Other chains start at dispersed values. With all terms fitted and a prior trial that disagrees with the data, the posterior of the scores can have several modes; compare chains (.chains) and the potential scale reduction factors.

Unbalanced trials. Missing plots and cells are completed by data augmentation (see bys_priors); an earlier trial with empty cells is completed by the EM algorithm before its fit.

Changes from version 0.2.0. The function no longer reads the earlier trial from objects in the workspace (n0, mu0, tau0, ...; it stopped with "object 'n0' not found" without them): the earlier trial is the argument .prior_data. The singular values were computed once and never sampled; tau1 held a precision drawn from a residual matrix that was never updated; the scores were drawn without their constraints and orthogonalised afterwards; the columns of delta1 were named for the genotypes. tau1 now holds the draws of the error variance \(\sigma^2\).

References

Perez-Elizalde, S., Jarquin, D. and Crossa, J. (2012). A general Bayesian estimation method of linear-bilinear models applied to plant breeding trials with genotype x environment interaction. Journal of Agricultural, Biological, and Environmental Statistics, 17(1), 15–37. doi:10.1007/s13253-011-0063-9

Crossa, J., Perez-Elizalde, S., Jarquin, D., Cotes, J. M., Viele, K., Liu, G. and Cornelius, P. L. (2011). Bayesian estimation of the additive main effects and multiplicative interaction model. Crop Science, 51(4), 1458–1469. doi:10.2135/cropsci2010.06.0343

Hoff, P. D. (2009). Simulation of the matrix Bingham-von Mises-Fisher distribution, with applications to multivariate and relational data. Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics, 18(2), 438–456. doi:10.1198/jcgs.2009.07177

Wood, A. T. A. (1994). Simulation of the von Mises Fisher distribution. Communications in Statistics - Simulation and Computation, 23(1), 157–164.

bayes_ammi_biplot, bys_priors, bys_interpret, bys_ls_ammi

Examples

data(cultivo2008)
data(cultivo2009)
fm3 <-
  bayes_ammi(
      .data       = cultivo2009
    , .y          = y
    , .gen        = entry
    , .env        = site
    , .rep        = rep
    , .nIter      = 300
    , .prior_data = cultivo2008
    , .n0         = NULL
    , .model      = "AMMI"
    , .k          = NULL
    , .burnin     = 100
    , .thin       = 1
    , .chains     = 1
    , .priors     = bys_priors(
          mu_mean     = 0
        , mu_var      = 1e+8
        , tau_mean    = 0
        , tau_var     = 1e+8
        , delta_mean  = 0
        , delta_var   = 1e+8
        , lambda_mean = 0
        , lambda_var  = 1e+8
        , nu          = 1
        , s2          = NULL
        )
    , .level      = 0.95
    , .seed       = 1
    , .align      = TRUE
    , .waic       = TRUE
    )
fm3
